question: Can a cross-validated, gradient-boosted regressor give lower and more uniform error than a standard MLP baseline when estimating a continuous physical quantity from robot-arm sensor readings on a public stand-in dataset?
method: OpenML kin8nm, one 80/20 split (fixed seed), inputs standardised on training data. Baseline: sklearn MLPRegressor. Improved: weighted blend of LightGBM (hyperparameters incl. linear leaves chosen by 5-fold CV on the training set, plus sine/cosine features) and the same MLP, with the blend weight chosen on out-of-fold training predictions. Test-set MAE is the main metric; mean over three seeds.
baseline: scikit-learn MLPRegressor, two hidden layers of 64 units, early stopping, standardised inputs and target; stands in for the paper's CNN-RNN.
improved: Ensemble: CV-tuned LightGBM (with linear leaves, sine/cosine features) blended with the baseline MLP; blend weight chosen by 5-fold CV on the training set only.
notes: kin8nm is a simulated robot-arm dataset, not contact-force data; it is a stand-in only. The paper's neuromorphic-camera CRNN was not reproduced; the MLP is a generic baseline. Single train/test split; seeds vary model randomness only. Hyperparameters and blend weight chosen by CV on training data; test set used once. The first LightGBM-only attempt did not beat the MLP on this smooth target, so tree leaves were made linear and the MLP was blended in. Secondary metrics are RMSE, R^2 and the std of absolute error (uniformity proxy); classification F1 does not apply to regression.
